Overview

Enterprise AI Platform (AI Base Framework) is a comprehensive enterprise AI platform designed with the vision: "Chỉ cần cắm AI vào hệ thống khác là có thể sử dụng được" (Just plug AI into other systems and it works). The platform provides ready-to-use AI capabilities that can be integrated into ERP, DMS, CRM, HRM, Workflow, and BI systems.

Key Features

1. Semantic Search & RAG Chatbot

  • Vector Search: Semantic search with pgvector HNSW index for high accuracy
  • Hybrid Search: Combines vector and keyword search for optimal results
  • RAG Pipeline: Retrieval Augmented Generation for accurate, source-cited answers
  • Document Processing: Upload, chunk (512 tokens), embed, and index documents automatically
  • Multi-language Support: Vietnamese and English

2. AI Agent & Tool Calling

  • Agent Orchestrator: Multi-step task planning and execution
  • Tool Registry: Dynamic tool registration and execution
  • Safety Guardrails: Enterprise security for AI actions
  • Human-in-the-loop Approval: Sensitive actions require human approval
  • Audit & Traceability: Full action logging and rollback support

3. Natural Language to SQL

  • NL to SQL Engine: Convert natural language questions to SQL queries
  • SQL Injection Protection: Query validation, only SELECT queries allowed
  • RBAC Integration: AI respects user permissions in database queries

4. Voice AI

  • Speech-to-Text: Whisper integration for voice input
  • Text-to-Speech: Voice output for AI responses
  • Voice Commands: Execute AI actions via voice

5. AI Gateway & Multi-Provider Support

  • Ollama (Local): 100% offline, llama3.2:3b, nomic-embed-text
  • OpenAI: GPT-4, GPT-3.5-turbo
  • Claude: Anthropic Claude models
  • Gemini: Google Gemini Pro
  • Azure OpenAI: Enterprise Azure integration
  • DeepSeek: Cost-effective AI
  • Dynamic Routing: Load balancing, fallback, cost-aware, latency-aware routing

6. Integration - MCP (Model Context Protocol)

  • MCP Server: AI-native protocol for external system integration
  • REST API & gRPC: Standard API integration
  • WebSocket: Real-time communication
  • Event-Driven: RabbitMQ-ready for async workflows

Architecture

High-Level Architecture

Client Layer (Web, Mobile, Voice, CLI)
         │
         ▼
API Gateway Layer (Auth, Rate Limiting, Tenant Resolution)
         │
         ▼
Platform Core (Modular Monolith)
├── Tenant Management Module
├── Auth & Security Module
├── AI Agent Runtime Module
├── AI Engine Core Module
├── Plugin Runtime Module
├── Workflow Engine Module
├── Document Pipeline Module
├── Search Engine Module
└── Integration Hub Module
         │
         ▼
AI Infrastructure Layer
├── AI Gateway (Router)
├── Embedding Engine
├── Vector Store
├── Model Registry
└── Tool Registry
         │
         ▼
AI Providers (Ollama, OpenAI, Claude, Gemini, Azure, DeepSeek)

Design Principles

  • Hybrid Architecture: Modular Monolith → Gradual Microservice Extraction
  • Plugin-based: Extensible for 3rd party integration
  • Agent-based: AI-native autonomous actions
  • Event-driven: Async communication patterns
  • Domain-Driven Design: Bounded contexts, shared kernel

Technology Stack

ComponentTechnology
Backend.NET 8, ASP.NET Core, MediatR, CQRS
FrontendNext.js 14, React 18, TailwindCSS, Zustand
DatabasePostgreSQL 16 + pgvector (Vector DB)
CacheRedis 7
Object StorageMinIO (S3-compatible)
LLM (Local)Ollama, llama3.2:3b, nomic-embed-text, whisper
LoggingSerilog, Seq
ContainerDocker, Docker Compose, Nginx

Security Features

  • JWT Authentication with refresh tokens
  • SQL Injection Protection with query validation
  • Prompt Injection Detection
  • Rate Limiting per user/tenant
  • RBAC (Role-Based Access Control)
  • Audit Logging for compliance
  • Human-in-the-loop Approval for sensitive actions
  • Zero Trust Architecture

Multi-Tenancy

  • Row-Level Security for tenant isolation
  • Per-tenant AI configuration
  • Tenant-specific rate limits
  • Configurable LLM models and prompts

Roadmap

  1. Phase 1 (Current): Core RAG, Semantic Search, Basic Chatbot
  2. Phase 2: AI Agent, Tool Calling, MCP Integration
  3. Phase 3: Voice AI, Multi-provider Gateway
  4. Phase 4: Enterprise Integration Hub, Plugin System
  5. Phase 5: Advanced Agentic AI, Autonomous Workflows

Vision

The goal is not just to build a single AI application, but to develop it into an Enterprise AI Platform that can be used across multiple business systems. The vision is: "Chỉ cần cắm AI vào hệ thống khác là có thể sử dụng được" — Just plug AI into other systems and it works.

This platform aims to serve as an AI Agent Platform, AI Copilot Platform, Internal AI Operating System, AI Integration Hub, and AI Automation Platform for enterprise systems including ERP, DMS, CRM, HRM, Workflow, and BI.

Introduction

This ASP.NET Core Web API project follows Clean Architecture, also known as Onion Architecture. It provides a reusable foundation with CQRS, dependency injection, logging, and API versioning.

Technologies and libraries

  • Framework: ASP.NET Core 6/7/8.
  • Application logic: MediatR implements CQRS, separating commands from queries.
  • Data access: Entity Framework Core handles writes, schema changes, and migrations. Dapper handles performance-sensitive reads.
  • Endpoints: Controllers and Carter-based Minimal APIs.
  • Validation and mapping: FluentValidation and AutoMapper.
  • Logging: Serilog.
  • Documentation: Swagger with API versioning.

Project structure

The source is divided into clear layers:

  • DemoCICD.API: The application entry point.
  • DemoCICD.Core: Business logic independent of external technology.
  • DemoCICD.Infrastructure: Database access and external services.
  • DemoCICD.Presentation: Presentation logic separated from the main API.

Key patterns

  1. CQRS separates read and write workflows.
  2. Global exception handling centralizes error responses.
  3. API versioning supports the evolution of endpoints.
  4. Swagger generates API documentation.
  5. Hybrid data access combines EF Core and Dapper.

Overview

A real-time chat application built with .NET 8, SignalR, PostgreSQL, and RabbitMQ. The Angular 17 frontend uses the SignalR client to receive live updates over WebSockets.

Database schema

  • Users: User information and online/offline status.
  • Conversations: Conversations between two users.
  • Messages: Sender, recipient, message content, and read status.

Authentication

The application supports registration and login using JWT. The implementation stores the token in localStorage and sends it through the Authorization bearer header, or the SignalR connection query string.

Chat API

  • User search: GET /api/Messages/users?search=keyword
  • Conversation list: GET /api/Messages/conversations
  • Paginated history: GET /api/Messages/conversation/{otherUserId}?page=1&pageSize=50
  • Send a message: POST /api/Messages/send

SignalR ChatHub

  • SendMessage: Sends a message from the client.
  • ReceiveMessage: Delivers new messages to the recipient.
  • UserOnline / UserOffline: Tracks presence.
  • MarkAsRead: Updates read status.

Message flow

  1. ChatComponent calls ChatService.sendMessage().
  2. ChatHub.SendMessage() processes the request.
  3. MessageService.SaveMessage() persists the message.
  4. ChatHub sends the message to the recipient through SignalR.
  5. The recipient handles the ReceiveMessage event.

Purpose

This e-commerce backend demonstrates microservices architecture and concepts from a distributed systems course.

System architecture

  • Frontend: Angular 17 on port 4200.
  • API Gateway: A RabbitMQ-based gateway on port 5010.
  • User Service: Load-balanced instances on ports 5001 and 5004.
  • Product Service: Load-balanced instances on ports 5002 and 5006.
  • Order Service: Load-balanced instances on ports 5003 and 5007.
  • Data: PostgreSQL with a separate database per service.
  • Messaging: RabbitMQ.
  • Logging: MongoDB Atlas.

Service responsibilities

User Service

JWT registration and login, listing and viewing users, profile updates, soft deletion, and delivery address management.

Product Service

Product listings and category search, product creation and updates, inventory management, discount pricing, tags, and reviews.

Order Service

Order creation, user order history, status updates, order items and status history, payment and shipping information, and RabbitMQ integration.

API Gateway

A single entry point routes requests through RabbitMQ with round-robin load balancing and Swagger documentation.

Technology stack

  • .NET 8 and Entity Framework Core.
  • PostgreSQL and MongoDB Atlas.
  • RabbitMQ and JWT authentication.
  • Angular 17 and Docker Compose.

Key takeaways

  1. Independent services with a database per service.
  2. Two instances per service for load distribution.
  3. Event-driven asynchronous communication.
  4. Documented APIs through Swagger.
  5. Containerized deployment through Docker Compose.

Overview

Phase 2 of the Document Management System for the Ministry of Finance, evolved from a monolithic multi-layer architecture into a full Microservices Architecture to support nationwide deployment across multiple government agencies.

System Architecture

The system consists of multiple layers:

1. External Layer

  • Client Applications: Web browsers, desktop clients
  • Mobile Applications: Native mobile apps for iOS/Android
  • Partner Systems: VBDQ (National Document Exchange), LDAP (Lightweight Directory Access Protocol)

2. Load Balancer - NGINX

  • Reverse proxy with SSL termination
  • Traffic distribution across multiple API Gateway instances
  • Rate limiting and request filtering

3. API Gateway - Ocelot

  • Single entry point for all client requests
  • JWT Authentication and Authorization
  • Request routing, rate limiting, and caching
  • Swagger documentation aggregation

4. Core Microservices

  • User Service: Authentication, authorization, LDAP integration, role management
  • Document Service: Document CRUD, version control, metadata management
  • Workflow Service: Dynamic workflow engine, approval routing, digital signatures
  • Report Service: Report generation, scheduling, export (PDF, Excel)
  • Notification Service: Email, SMS, Push notifications via RabbitMQ
  • Storage Service: File storage, S3-compatible storage, presigned URLs
  • Integration Service: VBDQ integration, LDAP sync, third-party APIs

5. Infrastructure Layer

  • RabbitMQ: Event-driven messaging, async communication between services, Dead Letter Queue for reliability
  • Redis Cache: Distributed caching, session management, rate limiting
  • ELK Stack: Elasticsearch, Logstash, Kibana for centralized logging, tracing, and monitoring
  • Docker Swarm: Container orchestration, service discovery, load balancing, rolling updates
  • Database Cluster: SQL Server cluster with read/write replication, failover clustering
  • Storage Cluster: S3-compatible object storage with redundancy

6. Security Layer

  • LDAP Integration: Unified authentication across government agencies
  • Digital Signature (Ky So): Hardware Security Module (HSM) for document signing, PDF signature verification
  • Role-Based Access Control: Fine-grained permissions per document type and agency

Technology Stack

ComponentTechnology
Backend Framework.NET, C#
API GatewayOcelot
Load BalancerNGINX
Message QueueRabbitMQ
Distributed CacheRedis
Logging & MonitoringELK Stack (Elasticsearch, Logstash, Kibana)
Container OrchestrationDocker Swarm
DatabaseSQL Server (Cluster)
Object StorageS3-Compatible (MinIO/AWS S3)
AuthenticationLDAP, JWT
Digital SignatureHSM, PDF Signature
Health MonitoringPrometheus, Health Checks

Key Highlights

  1. Microservices Architecture: 7 independent services, each with its own database
  2. Event-Driven Communication: RabbitMQ for async messaging, ensuring loose coupling
  3. High Availability: Docker Swarm with replicated containers, database clustering
  4. Centralized Logging: ELK Stack for log aggregation, search, and visualization
  5. Security by Design: LDAP integration, HSM-based digital signatures, JWT tokens
  6. Scalability: Horizontal scaling per service based on load
  7. Observability: Health checks, Prometheus metrics, distributed tracing

Challenges Solved

  • Multi-agency deployment: Multi-tenant architecture with LDAP-based authentication
  • Document integrity: HSM-based digital signatures ensure non-repudiation
  • High throughput: Redis caching + RabbitMQ for async processing handles 10,000+ concurrent users
  • Data consistency: Transactional Outbox Pattern ensures reliable event publishing
